questions.stem: Who owns the control flow in an agent?
options: The model decides what happens next.
The program decides what happens next.
Both the model and the program share control.
None of the above.

questions.stem: What is an agent according to the text?
options: An agent is a model using tools in a loop.
An agent is a simple program that runs once.
An agent is a tool that runs without feedback.
None of the above.
questions.source_quote: An agent is a model using tools in a loop.

questions.stem: According to the text, what is the role of the feedback loop in an agent?
options: The tool loop does the work, and the feedback loop checks it.
The feedback loop does the work, and the tool loop checks it.
Both loops are responsible for the same task.
None of the above.
questions.source_quote: The tool loop does the work. The feedback loop checks it.

questions.stem: What is the harness in an agent?
options: The harness is everything that is not the model.
The harness is a part of the model.
The harness is only used for testing.
None of the above.
questions.source_quote: The harness is everything that is not the model.

questions.stem: According to the text, when is a loop or a graph used in an agent workflow?
options: A loop is flexible and used for unknown steps.
A graph is predictable and used for known steps.
A loop is used for known steps, and a graph is used for unknown steps.
None of the above.
questions.source_quote: A loop is flexible. A graph is predictable.
